title: A Spark Neglected Burns the House
text:
Ivan Shcherbakov and his neighbor Gavrilo, called the Lame, had lived side by side for years in peace. Then one of Ivan's hens laid an egg in Gavrilo's yard. Ivan's daughter-in-law went to look for it and accused Gavrilo's family of taking it. Words flew between the women, then between the men. Gavrilo tore out a tuft of Ivan's beard, and Ivan's family struck back.

The quarrel grew year by year. There were lawsuits about the beard, about a broken cart, about anything that could be found. Ivan's old father, lying on the stove, kept begging his son to make peace before it was too late, but Ivan would not listen. At last Ivan got Gavrilo sentenced to a flogging, and Gavrilo muttered a threat about fire.

One night Ivan saw Gavrilo creeping by his shed with a burning wisp of straw. Instead of stamping out the flame, he ran after Gavrilo and seized him, but Gavrilo struck him on the head and knocked him senseless. When he came to, the fire had caught the thatch, and with the wind it spread until half the village was burned, Ivan's house among them.

His old father, carried out of the burning house, lay dying. He asked Ivan whose fault the fire was. Ivan admitted it was his own. The old man told him to say nothing about who had set it, and to forgive. Ivan obeyed. He never told, he made peace with Gavrilo, and the two families rebuilt and lived as good neighbors again.
lesson: Small grievances grow when pride keeps feeding them. Put out the spark of a quarrel early, while it costs only a little humility.
people: Ivan Shcherbakov, Gavrilo the Lame, Ivan's father
source: Leo Tolstoy, A Spark Neglected Burns the House (1885)
